extraction_metadata.scope_note: The full six-page case-series article was inspected. Case-level presentation, diagnostics, treatment, follow-up, discussion conclusions, and funding were atomized. Bibliography entries were not atomized. Background claims based on cited literature are tagged as secondary_background or secondary_synthesis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The report presents two young patients with plateau iris syndrome whose diagnoses arose during ophthalmic evaluation rather than from a planned case-series enrollment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We hereby present two case reports of plateau iris syndrome in young patients who came to an ophthalmologic consult by chance.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors distinguish plateau iris configuration from plateau iris syndrome by persistence or recurrence of gonioscopically confirmed angle closure after a patent iridotomy has relieved relative pupillary block.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: plateau iris syndrome ... refers to a post laser iridotomy condition in which a patent iridotomy has removed the relative pupillary block

atoms.canonical_statement: Plateau iris syndrome should be considered when intraocular pressure rises unexpectedly after an adequate peripheral iridotomy or iridectomy for angle-closure glaucoma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This condition must be considered in the differential diagnosis when the intraocular pressure rises unexpectedly following an adequate peripheral iridotomy

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 was a 43-year-old woman with moderate hyperopia who requested evaluation because of blurred vision in the right eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Mother (43 years old) ... requests a consult for herself as vision became blurry for some time in OD.

atoms.canonical_statement: In Case 1, right-eye visual acuity was 0.5 with +3.75 sphere and left-eye visual acuity was 1.0 with +4.5 sphere.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: AOVD= 0.5 cc (sph +3.75) AVOS= 1 cc (sph +4.5)

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 had severe right-eye visual-field loss, with mean deviation -30.88 dB and pattern standard deviation 6.88 dB, while the left visual field was reported as normal.
Case 1 had shallow peripheral but normal central anterior chamber depth, with intraocular pressure of 70 mmHg in the right eye and 36 mmHg in the left eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP-OD=70 mmHg IOP-OS=36 mmHg

atoms.canonical_statement: Fundus examination in Case 1 showed near-total right-eye optic-disc excavation with C/D=1 and a left-eye C/D ratio of 0.5/0.4.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: almost total excavation in right eye (C/D=1), whereas C/D ratio in OS was 0.5/0.4.

atoms.canonical_statement: Indentation gonioscopy in Case 1 showed the characteristic double-hump appearance, and the authors diagnosed plateau iris syndrome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: iris drapes over the ciliary body producing the double “hump” aspect on indentation

atoms.canonical_statement: Initial Case 1 therapy included intravenous 20% mannitol, systemic acetazolamide, and topical pilocarpine 2%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: prescribe manitol 20% ( iv) and acetazolamide plus Pilocarpine 2% topically.

atoms.canonical_statement: After intraocular pressure fell, Case 1 underwent peripheral laser iridotomy and argon laser peripheral iridoplasty.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a peripheral laser iridotomy (IP) was done along with an ALPI procedure

atoms.canonical_statement: After laser procedures in Case 1, intraocular pressure was 21 mmHg in the right eye and 15 mmHg in the left eye; additional beta-blocker and carbonic-anhydrase-inhibitor therapy was added for the right eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP after laser procedures was 21 mmHg in OD ... in OS the IOP was 15 mmHg

atoms.canonical_statement: At the later Case 1 follow-up after pilocarpine withdrawal, the angle was open through 360 degrees and intraocular pressure was 15 mmHg in both eyes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: last control showed open angle/ 3600 (Schaffer II or III) and IOP in both eyes was 15 mmHg.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 was a 29-year-old woman referred for bilateral juvenile decompensated glaucoma with ocular pain and decreased vision, worse in the right eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: B.E, female, 29 years old was referred ... for a diagnosis of OU Juvenile decompensated glaucoma.

atoms.canonical_statement: Before referral in Case 2, intraocular pressure was 38 mmHg in the right eye and 40 mmHg in the left eye; multidrug topical therapy reduced these values to 19 and 28 mmHg, respectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP-OD=38 mmHg, IOP-OS=40 mmHg ... Under this treatment IOP was OD=19 mmHg, OS-28mmHg.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the authors' examination in Case 2, intraocular pressure was 10 mmHg in the right eye and 19 mmHg in the left eye on multidrug therapy; central corneal thickness was 469 and 474 micrometers, respectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP-OD=10 mmHg ... IOP-OS=19 mmHg ... OD = 469μm, OS=474 μm

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had shallow peripheral but normal axial anterior chamber depth; gonioscopy showed 270 degrees of closure that opened to Schaffer IV through 360 degrees on indentation, with a positive double-hump sign.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: closed angle/ 2700 and open inferiorly ... by indentation the angle opened Schaffer IV/ 3600, “double hump” sign positive

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 visual fields showed right-eye MD -3.69 dB and PSD 5.15 dB and left-eye MD -5.65 dB and PSD 6.26 dB.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: MD=-3.69 dB, PSD=5.15 db ... MD=-5.65 dB, PSD=6.26 dB

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 fundus and OCT examinations showed retinal pigment epithelial irregularity, punctate flecks, and chronic sub-neurosensory macular fluid; the retina specialist suspected autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: diffuse irregularity of retinal pigment epithelium, dispersed punctate flecks and chronic accumulation of fluid beneath the neurosensory retina

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had prior laser peripheral iridotomies and later underwent bilateral argon laser peripheral iridoplasty because the left angle remained potentially occludable.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: She underwent a bilateral ALPI procedure without complication

atoms.canonical_statement: After bilateral argon laser peripheral iridoplasty in Case 2, repeat gonioscopy showed improved angle depth; at the last visit the angle was not judged occludable and intraocular pressure was 16 mmHg in each eye on beta-blocker plus carbonic-anhydrase-inhibitor therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: At the last visit, the angle does not appear to be occludable ... IOP-OD=16 mmHg; IOP-OS=16 mmHg (BB+CAI)

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors describe plateau iris syndrome as an uncommon form of primary angle-closure glaucoma that occurs more often in younger adults than pupillary-block angle closure and may be found incidentally.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Plateau iris syndrome is a relatively uncommon form of primary angle closure glaucoma that is seen more often in younger adults

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that a patent iridotomy may reduce angle-closure risk but may not alter anterior chamber anatomy, so periodic gonioscopy remains necessary even after successful iridotomy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Even after a successful iridotomy resulting in a well-open angle, periodic gonioscopy remains crucial

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that argon laser peripheral iridoplasty is the procedure of choice when the angle remains occluded after successful laser iridotomy and that regular gonioscopy remains necessary afterward.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Argon laser peripheral iridoplasty (ALPI) is the procedure of choice to effectively open an angle that remains occluded after successful laser iridotomy.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors highlight chance diagnosis, advanced previously unrecognized glaucoma, intermittent angle-closure features, and coexisting macular disease as notable features of their two cases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our cases exhibit certain particularities: diagnosis made by chance, advanced glaucoma that passed undiagnosed until advanced stage
